citation: Frances Benjamin Johnston, [Mrs. Fairbanks making address at the laying of the conerstone, Memorial Continental Hall, no. 5], platinum photograph, between 1905 and 1908 (title devised by the Library). Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, Frances Benjamin Johnston Collection, LOT 2910, LC-DIG-ppmsca-39000 (item 2015647074).
author: Frances Benjamin Johnston
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division. Master TIFF 39000u.tif (6064 x 4840), read at tile.loc.gov.
locator: The speakers' stand: Cornelia Cole Fairbanks standing to speak, at about five metres; beside her, seated, older women of the audience in dark bodices, white collars and trimmed hats.
rights_note: LOC rights advisory: 'No known restrictions on publication.' Used only as a reference picture the 1904 lady is judged against and for the cut of her day dress (T-3447); nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-07 (T-3447) from the master TIFF. Mrs. Fairbanks (Cornelia Cole Fairbanks, wife of Vice President Charles W. Fairbanks, as the Library's G. V. Buck portrait of her, item 2021636679, names her; a matron in middle age here) stands in a dark coat worn open over a pale front with a lace jabot falling from a high collar, white frills at the wrists, and a large hat heaped with pale plumes. Seated beside her, women of fifty and more wear dark bodices with high white collars or lace at the throat and hats trimmed with flowers and feathers. Washington, not Chicago; the LOC dates the print between 1905 and 1908.
note: One of the 1904 lady reference set's photographs (data/people_match/reference_sets/lady_1904.json): women of Frances Glessner's age and standing, out of doors in day dress.
what_it_supplies: a matron's day dress of the decade: a dark coat or bodice, a high white collar, a lace jabot at the throat
the large hats of the years, trimmed with plumes and flowers, worn on drawn-up hair
what_it_does_not_supply: anything about Chicago, the Glessner household or Frances M. Glessner; no likeness is asserted
